subtopic: API Rate Limiting (Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket)
question_text: What behavior distinguishes the Token Bucket rate-limiting algorithm from the Leaky Bucket algorithm?

options.text: Token bucket permits bursts of requests up to its capacity, whereas leaky bucket enforces a strictly smooth, constant output rate
Leaky bucket permits bursts, while token bucket drops all bursts
Token bucket requires distributed database locks
Leaky bucket is only applicable to UDP packets

answer_explanation: Token bucket allows accumulating tokens to be spent rapidly during spikes (burstiness). Leaky bucket processes requests at a constant, unyielding drip rate, buffering or dropping excess.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: Token bucket allows accumulating tokens to be spent rapidly during spikes (burstiness). Leaky bucket processes requests at a constant, unyielding drip rate, buffering or dropping excess.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
